A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Reddit psycholinguistic study. Their text, tables, equations, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including the graphical material on v2's final pages.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments, temporal analyses, permutation tests and supplementary TabPFN and Siamese-network results.

after.justification: V2 retains original classification results and reports additional demographic-proxy and feature-level analyses.

M1.justification: The core pipeline remains averaged 110-dimensional LIWC features, Random Forest classification and SHAP analysis. Auxiliary modeling changes: v1's shared-encoder Siamese procedure for comparing pre/post-engagement representations is removed, while v2 introduces weighted subreddit embeddings for demographic checks. These embeddings do not replace the classifier's LIWC inputs.

E1.justification: The 22 mainstream communities, 2013-2023 classification coverage and alternative target communities remain unchanged; the dataset tables retain identical values. V2 adds auxiliary coverage of conspiracy-engaged users' complete Reddit histories, exceeding two billion contributions, for demographic-proxy analysis.

E2.justification: TabPFN, random/permutation controls and pooled-versus-community-specific Random Forest comparisons remain. The TabPFN figure is identical across versions. The removed Siamese experiment tested a separate temporal-similarity question rather than serving as a comparator in these retained classification comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds a demographic evaluation protocol comparing weighted user embeddings with subreddit reference embeddings and relating their differences to classification gains. The reported subreddit-ranking snapshot changes from April to June 2025, without establishing reruns. Core classification settings remain, while the temporal-exclusion and Siamese evaluation setups disappear.

E4.justification: V2 adds demographic-confounding checks and detailed feature-level SHAP analyses, including Table 1 and the final appendix plots. It removes v1's 6-24-month exclusion-window and Siamese change-detection analyses. Activity stratification, TabPFN and temporal-quintile checks remain; the PCA analysis is relocated, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: V2 introduces Pearson-correlation estimation and a shaded band around the fitted trend in Figure 7, without specifying the band's construction or confidence level. Both versions retain five negative-class samplings and 100 label permutations; there is no evidence of increased classification replication.

E6.justification: New results include demographic distributions, the Pearson correlation of -0.01 in Figure 7, and feature-frequency, direction and ranking results in Table 1 and the SHAP plots. Exclusion-window and Siamese results are removed. Shared headline results retain 0.87 median classification accuracy and 0.76 pooled-model accuracy.

T1.justification: V1's explicit causal DAG and associated formalized hypotheses are dropped, together with the normalized time/activity definitions in Equations 1-2. V2 retains the quintile procedure descriptively and preserves the permutation p-value formula. No new theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds a pre-existing conspiratorial mindset, prediction years before participation and challenges to platform-driven radicalization. V2 removes these prominent conclusions and centers its contribution on observable engagement differences and community-dependent language. Context dependence was already reported in v1, but the principal research question and claim scope are substantially narrowed.

C2.justification: V2 distinguishes participation from underlying belief, explicitly leaves causal direction unresolved and replaces the platform-versus-individual responsibility argument with contextual moderation discussion. It expands profiling-risk qualifications and adds demographic and feature interpretations. Its new interpretation of LIWC 'mental' as reasoning conflicts with Appendix B.3's mental-health definition.

D1.justification: V2 adds hardware specifications, processing/training runtimes and a repository link in Appendix B.2. Section 3.3 clarifies user-disjoint splitting and training-only normalization/tuning, without establishing a changed implementation. V1's Siamese implementation recipe and detailed pre/post representation construction are omitted, although some pre/post result plots remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated review of detection, participation pathways and linguistic research, including new citations to Corso et al. (2025a) and Diab et al. (2024). It removes much of v1's intervention and selective-exposure positioning, including Costello et al. (2024) and Stroud (2008), and refocuses the contribution on contextual language analysis.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and discussion are extensively rewritten. Methods move before results, a Related Work section is introduced, and the two-study narrative becomes a unified study with temporal robustness material distributed between the main text and appendices. Ethics and limitations receive separate headings.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially different two-column layout, replaces the causal DAG with a workflow diagram, moves the PCA plot into the main text and relocates temporal-quintile plots to the appendix. It adds demographic and SHAP displays and Table 1, while removing aggregate pre/post, exclusion-window and Siamese figures.

improvement.justification: V2 better aligns its main claims with observational evidence by narrowing v1's mindset/radicalization conclusions and qualifying engagement labels. Clearer training procedures and resource/repository disclosures improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by missing explanations for retained pre/post plots and the new 'mental' interpretation error. Both versions also retain the inconsistency between reporting p < 0.001 and specifying 100 permutations, whose stated minimum p-value is 0.0099.
